subject: english-language

moments.title: Language and Power
moments.body: 1989: Norman Fairclough's 'Language and Power' published. Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) examines how language reproduces and challenges social power. Drawing on Foucault, Halliday's systemic functional linguistics, and Bakhtin, Fairclough analyses texts from political speech, advertising and media.
moments.takeaway: CDA is now a major branch of applied linguistics. Fairclough's three-dimensional framework (text, discourse practice, social practice) is widely taught.

moments.title: Discourse and Social Change, Critical Discourse Analysis
moments.body: Fairclough's subsequent books develop the framework. 'Discourse and Social Change' (1992) and 'Critical Discourse Analysis' (1995) extend the analysis. Ruth Wodak's discourse-historical approach and Teun van Dijk's socio-cognitive approach are parallel CDA traditions.
moments.takeaway: CDA's combination of linguistic analysis and social critique has been embraced by sociolinguists, sociologists, media studies.

moments.title: Critiques and extensions
moments.body: Widdowson and others have criticised CDA for projecting ideological readings onto texts without sufficient linguistic constraint. Defenders argue the framework is sufficiently rigorous when applied properly. Modern CDA extends to multimodal analysis (image, sound) and digital discourse.
moments.takeaway: Modern critical discourse analysis remains a major teaching and research framework — for political discourse, media, business communication and educational analysis.

now.title: Discourse and power
now.body: CDA is taught at A-level and in many university courses. Application to political speech (Brexit, Trump), corporate communications, journalism is continuous. Modern multimodal CDA examines images, videos and social media alongside text.
now.open_questions: Is CDA scientific or political critique? Both, on its own terms. Whether the political stakes are appropriate for the linguistic methodology is contested.

reflection: A 1989 book opened the major late-20th-century framework for analysing language and power. CDA's combination of linguistic technique and social critique has shaped how generations of students and researchers approach language in its political dimensions.
